title: Full counters, not masked indexes
body: Empty is head == tail, full is tail - head == size, on 64-bit counters that only grow; the mask is applied only to address a slot.
rationale: The classic masked design cannot tell empty from full without sacrificing a slot; with full counters every slot is usable and the test stays correct across a wrap.

title: 64-bit counters
body: The two counters are uint64_t whatever the payload's width.
rationale: A 32-bit counter wraps in 71 minutes at 10^6 hand-offs a second; a 64-bit one in about 584,000 years; the cost of the wider arithmetic is nothing beside the atomic traffic.

title: Power-of-two capacity
body: The capacity must be a power of two so that index & (size - 1) addresses the slot.
rationale: A mask instead of a division on every push and pop; the customer's capacities are powers of two already.

title: Head and tail on separate cache lines
body: The control block aligns head and tail on SPSC_CACHELINE and is allocated with aligned_alloc at that alignment.
rationale: Each side writes one counter; on one line every write would invalidate the other core's copy.

title: Refuse lock-backed atomics
body: The library checks the two actual counters with atomic_is_lock_free at creation and refuses the ring; the project's builds also define SPSC_REQUIRE_ALWAYS_LOCK_FREE for a compile-time refusal.
rationale: C11 allows _Atomic uint64_t to be implemented with a lock; a lock would break wait-freedom silently.

title: An int payload
body: The ring stores int, the type of a file descriptor, not void*.
rationale: The customer carries descriptors; MPSCring, the sibling, carries pointers for the many-producer case.

title: The least ordering that is enough
body: Each side reads its own counter relaxed, the other side's with acquire, and publishes its own with release; no sequentially consistent operation and no fence.
rationale: Each counter has one writer; acquire/release on the pair is exactly the happens-before the hand-off needs (Lamport's ring, in C11 terms).
